L0@P0: FHWA-SA-21-042
L1@P0: Roundabouts
L2@P0: The modern roundabout is an intersection with a circular configuration that
L3@P0: safely and efficiently moves traffic. Roundabouts feature channelized, curved
L4@P0: approaches that reduce vehicle speed, entry yield control that gives right-ofway to circulating traffic, and counterclockwise flow around a central island
L5@P0: that minimizes conflict points. The net result of lower speeds and reduced
L6@P0: conflicts at roundabouts is an environment where crashes that cause injury or
L7@P0: fatality are substantially reduced.
L8@P0: Roundabouts are not only a safer
L9@P0: type of intersection; they are also
L10@P0: efficient in terms of keeping people
L11@P0: moving. Even while calming traffic,
L12@P0: they can reduce delay and queuing
L13@P0: when compared to other intersection
L14@P0: alternatives. Furthermore, the lower
L15@P0: vehicular speeds and reduced
L16@P0: conflict environment can create
L17@P0: a more suitable environment for
L18@P0: walking and bicycling.
L19@P0: Roundabouts can be implemented
L20@P0: in both urban and rural areas under
L21@P0: a wide range of traffic conditions.
L22@P0: They can replace signals, twoway stop controls, and all-way
L23@P0: stop controls. Roundabouts are an
L24@P0: effective option for managing speed
L25@P0: and transitioning traffic from highspeed to low-speed environments,
L26@P0: such as freeway interchange ramp
L27@P0: terminals, and rural intersections
L28@P0: along high-speed roads.
